_comment: Feature flags for the 2026-04-19 sprint. Every key defaults to false in backend/feature_flags.py. Flip a value to true here to enable the feature in the running deployment. Unknown keys are ignored with a console warning.
_comment_picks_league_horizon: 2026-08-19 feedback #355 (BUG, TradesHome, v1.15.0): '2029 picks showing on sleeper league without 2029 picks available'. Sleeper carries exactly THREE consecutive rookie classes anchored to the first class that has not yet been drafted - verified live against every prod league on 2026-08-19: league 1312140920132497408 (2026 draft pre_draft) has traded picks in 2026/2027/2028 and none in 2029, while league 1312583962966650880 (2026 draft complete) does have 2029 traded picks. sync_draft_picks instead built a fixed [current_season .. current_season+3] grid, which is a 4th class for exactly the pre-draft leagues; the post-draft ones were already right because #228 shifted their anchor by one. Result: 339 of 2651 served cards (12.8% of all, 23.2% of pick-bearing cards) offered a phantom 2029 pick, all in the operator league, and 12.9% of recorded like/pass outcomes landed on one. D-079 (flat round-1 pick values across years) made the generator reach for far-dated firsts freely, which is why the defect surfaced now. ON = the grid comes from draft_status.pick_horizon, widened by any season the platform itself reports a traded pick for (existence proof, capped at PICK_HORIZON_MAX_CLASSES so a malformed feed cannot re-open the defect). OFF = the historical seasons_ahead window, byte-identical to today. Write-side only - no route, payload or read path changes, and because the sync is a replace-sync the rows converge on the next session_init either way. Scope is the Sleeper platform sync only: MFL enumerates real picks from its futureDraftPicks export and has no phantom exposure, ESPN has no platform pick source at all, and the manual assignment grid (seed_pick_grid, _ASSIGNMENT_SEASONS_AHEAD = current+3) is a recorded operator decision wired into the assignment progress denominator - left untouched and logged as Q-022.
_comment_pick_slot_labels: 2026-08-19 operator feedback (screen TradesHome, v1.15.0): 'For 2026 picks, we should present them as actual draft pick slot rather than a generic 2026 round pick'. D-090. picks.slot_labels makes an OWNED pick's label read '2026 1.08' instead of '2026 1st' once its league's CURRENT-season draft order is known. It is a DISPLAY flag and nothing else: pick_pool_value, GENERIC_PICK_SEEDS, tier bands, the stored draft_picks.pool_value and every engine input are byte-identical in BOTH states, because the slot is not a pricing input under this change (whether an early 1st should be worth more than a mid 1st is a separate, unbuilt pricing question — Q-023). Resolution has two zero-egress sources: a Sleeper league's draft_order, which already rides the /league/<id>/drafts payload the owned-pick sync fetches for #228, composed with the rosters map that sync already holds; and a user-assigned (ESPN) league's stored pick_assignment_settings.order. MFL is unsupported — its order needs an authed draftResults fetch nobody on the label path makes. Three deliberate refusals, all producing today's generic label rather than a guess: an unset draft_order (Sleeper's pre-draft slot_to_roster_id identity map is NEVER read — the D5 rule), any season other than the stamped one (#273 — nobody knows 2027's order), and a snake draft with reversal_round set (unverifiable parity, mirroring draft_board_service._pick_no). The order is stored on leagues.draft_slot_order and the SLOT is never stored, because renumbering must never touch an owner (D18). OFF = all five owned-pick label sites (_roster_eveners, /api/league/picks, _pick_labels_by_id, _owned_pick_assets, _power_picks_by_owner) emit the pre-D-090 string byte-for-byte; the column is still written, so flipping it back ON needs no re-sync. Ships ON, matching its two nearest siblings picks.owned_sync and picks.rank_year_labels; under D-056 it carries no runtime proof beyond the manual TestFlight checklist in the scope block.
_comment_compressed_board: 2026-08-15 field bug on the operator's real league FFV3 (docs/plans/compressed-board-pool/scope.md): three of four BOARDED leaguemates produced zero trade cards at any per-opponent budget while mutually positive trades existed (Gibbs <-> A.J. Brown scored min-side surplus +3682 against a floor of 60). Two independent defects. trade.pool_calibration fixes the v3 candidate-pool prune, which ranked by the raw divergence `_vo - _uv`; because elo_to_value is exponential, an opponent board sitting uniformly lower than the user's (those three had median Elo ~1220 vs the consensus 1347, floor-pinned at 1200) deflates high-Elo players far more than low-Elo ones, so every tradeable stud sorted BELOW the user's worthless bench and the top-12 pool filled with junk. ON = the opponent's value space is rescaled onto the user's before differencing, making the pool ORDER invariant to a board-wide offset that carries no preference information; prune ordering only, surplus/fairness math untouched. trade.divergence_fallback fixes the compounding defect in trade_service: the boarded/unboarded branch was if/else with no fall-through, so a boarded member yielding zero divergence cards got no consensus fallback either and vanished from the deck -- ranking a little made a leaguemate a worse trade partner than never ranking at all. Both were built DARK and flipped ON by explicit operator instruction on 2026-08-15, after the read-only prod field verification in the scope block (gdubs10 0->5 divergence with pool_calibration; MangoPatti and Bcork 0->5 consensus with divergence_fallback; the healthy board unchanged). Each flag is its own kill switch and setting either back to false is deploy-free. TWO ACCEPTED CONSEQUENCES, both operator-acknowledged at flip time: (1) a member with has_rankings=true can now carry basis:'consensus' cards; (2) generation stops once the deck reaches global_target = max(30, max_per_opponent*6) and boarded members are visited FIRST, so opponents after the break contribute nothing -- rescued boarded members DISPLACE unranked members' consensus cards. NOTE the target is a stop-when-reached threshold checked AFTER each opponent's whole batch is appended, not a truncation, so the deck can overshoot by up to max_per_opponent-1 (post-deploy FFV3 read: 34 cards, not 30). Card counts are field-verified; card QUALITY is not, and all field data is from FFV3 alone -- watch the first real decks.
_comment_trade_gen_v2: 2026-08-16 matchmaking research item 2 (docs/research/matchmaking/ rounds 1-2; scope: docs/plans/matchmaking-engine/trade-gen-v2-scope.md). trade_gen.v2 routes TradeService.generate_trades to backend/trade_gen_v2.py, the divergence-driven staged pipeline: partner+centerpiece selection by board divergence (want/accept boards as filters) -> bounded return-package search around the centerpiece (max 3 assets+picks per side) -> hard gates IN ORDER (roster feasibility both sides -> dual-board epsilon-gain on each side's OWN board with a non-linear consolidation discount so junk can't stuff a package -> consensus fairness band) -> rank by joint gain, tiebreak surplus-split symmetry -> empirical-Bayes acceptance-prior multiplier -> league-level exposure cap+floor shaping -> MESO return-package variants + structured two-sided rationale on the cards. Built DARK alongside the v2/v3 engine, never replacing it: OFF (default) = the module is never imported and every existing generation path is byte-identical. Divergence-only by design; unranked opponents keep the flag-off engine's consensus path. Tunables are the gen2_* model_config keys (docs/config-reference.md).
_comment_presentment_rules: 2026-08-16 G6 feedback wave (#304 #336 #339 #340 #341; docs/feedback/items/304-positional-need-filter/). trade.presentment_rules gates the v1-path construction rules (R1 overpay ceiling, R2 per-position net cap, R3 pick-is-the-gap band), the untargeted-deck need gate (R5, targeted jobs bypass server-side), the windowless awaiting/matched exclusion (R4, also applied to likes-you injection), and the presentment-tripwire logging. LAUNCHES ON (operator decision Q-G6-3: tester-filed bugs against live behavior; merged only after the DB-1/DB-2 kill-rate bands + code-walk proof passed). Per-rule deploy-free kill switches are the model_config knobs (max_overpay_frac<=0, pos_net_cap=0, pick_gap_frac=0, need_gate_min_value<=0); this flag is the one-line group revert and R4's only switch. OFF => every generation path byte-identical to pre-G6.
_comment_outlook_odds: 2026-08-19 OPERATOR OVERRIDE (verbatim: 'Outlook odds should be visible'), reversing the same session's D-093 recommendation to keep it dark; recorded as D-094. Lights the #169 League-Summary season-outlook layer that has been built-but-dark since f27c0f5 (2026-08-11): the collapsed one-line 'your outlook' strip (D-025) and the full section behind it, plus GET /api/league/outlook, which 404s while this is false. WHAT IS AND IS NOT LICENSED BY THIS FLIP. playoff_pct renders ONLY as the three-band chip (likely/tossup/unlikely) whose thresholds, labels and semantic pos/warn/neg colors are a cross-client invariant (docs/cross-client-invariants.md S Playoff outlook bands) - never a bare percentage. title_pct is SERVED BUT UNRENDERABLE at any week in any form, banded or numeric: that is not a calibration judgement but an absence of demonstrated skill (pooled +4.2%, 90% CI [-13.1%, +20.0%]; 3 of 6 backtested league-seasons worse than climatology; 8 predictions above 0.4 containing one champion). The week-6+ rounded-percentage option stays OFF - OUTLOOK_WEEK6_PERCENT_ENABLED in LeagueSummaryScreen.tsx is a SEPARATE operator risk call on pooled, non-week-stratified calibration, and lighting this flag is not lighting it. PRESEASON POSTURE (today, completed_weeks == 0): meta.beta is true, so the surface shows bands and row order only, with NO win-loss numbers - a projected record is the same false-precision point estimate as a percentage in another unit - and carries the 'Projected - preseason - beta' ribbon. Bands at week 0 are what the evidence supports: preseason skill excludes zero (+21.3%, CI [+2.9, +39.1]), while the finer granularity does not (calibration-combined-2026-08-10.md S7-S8). PLATFORM: Sleeper only. backend/outlook/league_state.py registers ESPN/MFL/Fleaflicker as NotImplemented stubs, so the client gates the query on outlookSupported (LeagueSummaryScreen.tsx) and those leagues render no section at all rather than a 501 - honest absence, already built, no error state. EVIDENCE: the Maestro flow this lighting used to owe (NEXT.md item 7) is WAIVED by the operator 2026-08-19 and was already void under D-056; the standing guard is instead mobile/tests/check-outlook-bands.js, which pins the three thresholds, the band-to-color map, and that no client reads title_pct. OFF = every outlook surface disappears and the endpoint 404s again; the flip is deploy-free via POST /api/feature-flags/reload and needs no client release.
_comment_outlook_trade_impact: 2026-08-19 feedback #357 (TradeCalculator, idea): 'here's 6 extra PPG this year which raises your playoff odds to X'. outlook.trade_impact adds an additive `outlook_impact` block to POST /api/trade/evaluate: the caller's playoff odds BEFORE vs AFTER this specific trade. Reverses D-025, which deferred the card odds block on a backend cost that was never measured; measured 2026-08-19 it was a ~20x overestimate for a DELTA. The simulator seeds off the LEAGUE not the rosters (stable_hash(league_id) ^ config_seed), so both runs draw the identical random stream - common random numbers - which buys two measured properties: an unchanged roster yields a delta of EXACTLY 0.0 (bit-identical, so a trade that changes nothing can never show a spurious shift), and the delta is MORE stable than either absolute it is drawn from (0.4 points of movement across a 10x sim reduction vs 1.05 for the absolute). Hence DELTA_SIM_COUNT=2000 not 10000: within 0.3 points of the 10000-sim answer at ~112ms instead of ~689ms, with the baseline cached per (league, basis) so a 30-card deck pays 31 simulations rather than 60. RENDERING IS NOT LICENSED BY THIS FLAG: title_pct is neither computed nor returned, and the client shows band-to-band movement rather than a bare percentage - see docs/cross-client-invariants.md. SLEEPER ONLY (backend/outlook/league_state.py registers the other platforms as NotImplemented stubs) and Mode-B only; every other case omits the block entirely rather than guessing. OFF = the block is absent and /api/trade/evaluate is byte-identical. LIT 2026-08-19 by operator instruction, same day it was built. UNLIKE outlook.odds, this one DOES need a client release: CardImpactBlock is new code and is not in build 121. Two live costs accepted at flip time, both real: (1) the FIRST fronted card of a session pays the LeagueState build plus the baseline simulation, not just the ~112ms with-trade run - the per-(league,basis) cache has a 15-min TTL, so a cold deck is slower than a warm one; (2) nobody has seen this block on a device. Kill switch is deploy-free via POST /api/feature-flags/reload and costs only the block - /api/trade/evaluate stays correct with the flag off.
_comment_trades_team_review: 2026-08-19 feedback #357/#358/#359 (jonbonjourvi, v1.15.0): 'an idiot version of wtf do I do next with this team'. trades.team_review gates GET /api/league/team-review and the mobile Team Review flow: six stepped beats (standing / window / depth / divergence / partners / plan), each one finding, one plain read, one action. FOUR OF THE SIX ACTIONS WRITE league_preferences (team_outlook, acquire_positions, trade_away_positions) through the EXISTING POST /api/league/preferences - no new write route - so the flow's exit is a deck reshaped by what the user just agreed to rather than a report. The backend is a pure composer (backend/team_review.py) over five functions that already ship: compute_power_rankings, optimal_starter_slots, infer_team_outlook, analyze_roster_strengths, compute_consensus_gap. It computes NO new number, so there is no new model to calibrate. meta.beats_skipped is authoritative - the client renders beats minus beats_skipped in beats order and never decides for itself that a beat is empty. Degrades rather than fails: non-Sleeper and preseason leagues lose only the PPG card (with the reason named), a thin board skips the divergence beat, a 2-team league skips partners. The playoff band on the standing beat rides outlook.odds and is omitted entirely when that is off - the two flags are independent kill switches. OFF = the route 404s, the entry card does not render, and every existing path is byte-identical. LIT 2026-08-19 by operator instruction. REQUIRES A CLIENT RELEASE: TeamReviewScreen and TeamReviewEntryCard are new code and are NOT in build 122 (built from 639df3b, before PR #149 merged), so the backend route goes live on merge but nothing renders until the next TestFlight build. Evidence: 15 backend tests (backend/tests/test_team_review.py, three sabotages) plus mobile/tests/check-team-review.js (7 assertions, three sabotage-proven: a local FeedbackFAB, a Review chip added to the mode bar, and a renamed beat testID).

_comment_espn_send: 2026-08-12 graduates the ESPN trade-write path per D-026, which reversed the old categorical NO-GO to a GATED go. Both blocking probes passed: the DynastyProcess crosswalk's espn_id IS the write-API playerId (live-verified 4/4 against two real ffl proposals), and a bare POST carrying only espn_s2+SWID plus the static x-fantasy-* headers — no CSRF or per-session token — returned 409 TRAN_INVALID_TRADE_TEAM_COUNT, a trade-domain validation error only reachable AFTER auth succeeds. _comment_onboarding: Onboarding redesign (docs/plans/onboarding-conversion/plan.md v2.1). onboarding.v2 is the master kill-switch: a feature is live iff onboarding.v2 AND its own flag. PHASE A (2026-08-15, docs/business/product/2026-08-14-open-access-onboarding.md §5): onboarding.landing, onboarding.trades_first, onboarding.quickset_prompt, onboarding.league_autoskip, onboarding.apple_save_moment and landing.try_before_sync are now TRUE by default — the built v2 flow is the product, not an experiment overlay. The remaining onboarding.* keys (share_sheet, rank_routing, demo_bridge, guided_layer, keep_warm) still ship dark. analytics.client_events sits OUTSIDE the master — it starts the pre-redesign baseline capture and should be flipped true first. _comment_guide_v2: Guided Onboarding v2 (docs/plans/guided-onboarding-v2/scope.md §2). onboarding.guide_v2 gates EVERY v2 addition to The Analyst tour: the declarative eligibility layer, the guide's membership in the interrupt arbiter, all new beats (N1, N2, N4, N5, N6.1, N8, N9) and the copy changes riding the new script fields. It sits UNDER the onboarding.v2 master like its siblings, and it is the rollback lever: false = byte-identical to pre-v2-build behavior, config-only (POST /api/feature-flags/reload, no deploy). _comment_growth_tier_board_share: 2026-08-11 P1 audit remediation, operator decision D-P1-12 (docs/plans/audit-p1-remediation/DECISIONS-p1.md): sharing of rankings / tier boards is NOT a product surface and must not be live in any form. _comment_growth_invite_join_link: P0-3 invite deep link. EMITTER ONLY, default OFF. _comment_league_picks_always_counted: 2026-08-10 feedback #293/#294 (docs/feedback/items/293-picks-in-subsets/), AMENDED 2026-08-12 by operator decision (docs/feedback/items/300-league-rankings-trade-candidates/status-mobile.md). SHIPPED ON 2026-08-10; this is the kill switch for a REVERSAL of shipped behavior on the League rankings chart (mobile LeagueSummaryScreen, route LeagueRankings). The screen shipped with the rule 'picks are neither starters nor bench', so a team's draft capital was counted ONLY in the All subset with no position filter, and evaporated the moment the user tapped Starters, Bench, or any position pill - a rebuilding team holding four 1sts ranked like a team holding none. Operator ruling: 'I'm talking about picks for value' - pick value is subset-independent and filter-independent. ON = activeTotal adds the team's full picks.value in ALL THREE subsets and whenever PICKS is in the position filter; the neutral Picks bar segment, the legend swatch and the Picks pill render in every subset; the drill-in 'Draft capital' group renders under every subset and filter; and three hint strings stop claiming 'only' ('Best starting lineup + draft capital.', 'Bench + draft capital.', '... starter + picks value'). A consequence the UI states rather than hides: with picks counted in both, Starters + Bench deliberately no longer partition All (the two are never summed on screen). OFF = every one of those paths takes its pre-#293 branch and the screen is byte-identical to the shipped 1.11.0 build, including the raw 'PICKS' enum in the filtered hint line. 2026-08-12 AMENDMENT - THE TWO togglePos RULES ARE REMOVED, in BOTH flag states. #294 also made the flag-ON pill toggle auto-add PICKS on the first position tap (rule A) and clear the filter to All when removing the last core position (rule B). Operator: 'All leagues have picks. They should not be selected along with a position filter. Only by explicit user action.' The original reasoning is preserved rather than deleted, because this is a deliberate reversal taken with it on the record: rule A existed so that 'selecting a position must not remove draft capital'. The counter-reading that won is that because EVERY league carries picks, rule A fired for effectively every user on every first position tap - which makes pick inclusion a default, not a choice - and a position filter should mean that position. Rule B fell with it: its stated job was to stop the user being stranded in 'a picks-only ranking they never asked for', a state only rule A could produce unasked; with rule A gone every PICKS in the filter is a hand-tapped pill, so clearing to All would discard an explicit choice. #294's note that separating those cases 'would need a hidden the-user-chose-picks-by-hand state axis' is obsolete for the same reason - removing rule A makes the axis unnecessary. togglePos is now a plain, FLAG-INDEPENDENT toggle: this flag no longer gates it in either direction, and mobile/tests/check-picks-subset-invariance.js assertions 3e-3h pin that absence structurally. The flag still governs everything else listed above (12 gated expressions, was 14). The pill invariant is unchanged and now rests on activeTotal alone: whenever the filter is non-empty, the Picks pill's selected state is exactly equal to whether pick value is in the chart. The switch is read ONCE into a single boolean and gates the whole set atomically - never a subset of it, because bar SEGMENT heights are percentages of their own sum while the bar's HEIGHT comes from the team total, so a partially-gated build would grow the bar by the pick value while silently stretching the four position segments to fill it. No backend behavior rides this flag: picks.value and pool_value are byte-identical in both states, the payload is unchanged, and _power_picks_by_owner takes no basis argument, so both value bases carry the same per-team constant and the #208/#248 tick-and-delta overlay is invariant either way.
_comment_league_pos_candidates: 2026-08-12 feedback #300 (docs/feedback/items/300-league-rankings-trade-candidates/, frozen design in operator-answers-2026-08-12.md). Two keys, both flipped ON by operator direction on 2026-08-12 in the same change that shipped them - they did NOT bake dark. The operator also waived the pre-ship simulator gate and the Maestro execution for this ship, so the first runtime exercise of this code is TestFlight itself: the 44pt hit-slop treatment on the drill-in rows, the divider, and the rule-A removal have never run on a device or simulator. Kill switch: set either key false. league.pos_candidates: on the mobile League rankings list, when EXACTLY ONE core position is selected, draw one labelled median divider on the playoff-cutline pattern - teams above it are sellers, below are buyers, the caller's own team stays in the list as the anchor. The bottom 33% carry a 'Buyer' label and the top 33% a 'Seller' label (band = round(team_count * 0.33)); the middle is unlabelled, but the LINE, not the label, is the direction rule for every team. Tapping a team opens a stacked-roster drill-in (never side-by-side columns) showing your players if the team sits below the line and theirs if above. The divider renders ONLY on a single-position filter - multi-position has no single median to draw. OFF = the list renders exactly as it does today. league.player_trade_handoff: the drill-in row actions - 'Offer' on your own players (pins give), 'Target' on the other team's (pins receive) - which route to the trade finder and REPLACE existing pins. OFF = rows carry no action, so the divider can ship and be evaluated without the write-side handoff. Both keys are read by the mobile client; the backend serves the new `medians` field on GET /api/league/power-rankings UNFLAGGED, because it is additive (it changes no existing key), costs one sort per position per request, and a flag-on/field-absent state would be a strictly worse contract for the client to reason about.
